races.name: Auto Services Perth Supporting Dundee Bairns Novices' Limited Handicap Steeple Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Dunkerque
runners_data.note: Boasts a formidable OR-132 and has won four of his last five starts, all on Good ground at distances between 20f and 22f — the 2m4f trip here is squarely in his wheelhouse; Sean Quinlan retains the ride and the Candlish yard is 1/13 in the 14-day window, a minor flag but not alarming given this horse's own recent dominance.

runners_data.name: Follow Your Luck
runners_data.note: Brian Hughes's mount naturally leads and will enjoy a completely uncontested break in front — his sole win on similar going (Good) and two previous wins on Soft suggest he handles the surface, but his OR-122 and status as a 5-year-old novice chaser represent a significant class gap versus Dunkerque; the Neville yard is 0/7 in 14 days.

races.paceDynamic: Follow Your Luck (Brian Hughes) is the sole confirmed front-runner in a two-horse field and will lead from the outset at a pace entirely of his own choosing — with no rival capable of, or likely to, dispute that lead, Hughes can set whatever tempo suits his mount. Dunkerque (Sean Quinlan) is a prominent racer who will track Follow Your Luck closely throughout, meaning this amounts to a procession-style contest with the shape set from the first fence. The decisive question is whether Follow Your Luck's stamina and jumping hold up over 2m4f under a penalty-free weight advantage, or whether Dunkerque's superior class, recent winning form, and big-race record eventually overwhelms him in the straight. This race shape — a lone, uncontested leader controlling tempo — most favours a genuine front-runner who can dictate and conserve energy, giving Follow Your Luck a structural advantage, though Dunkerque's class edge and consistent winning form on Good ground means he remains the primary threat throughout.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Leader Dictates, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Follow Your Luck controls tempo throughout and jumps cleanly, conserving enough reserves to repel Dunkerque's challenge.
scenarios.body: Hughes sets a measured gallop that drains Dunkerque's finishing kick, and Follow Your Luck's course-compatible profile on Good ground (1W from 3 on similar) enables him to see out the trip. The uncontested lead is the structural engine here — no pressure early means maximum stamina reserves late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Dunkerque Class Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If Dunkerque's superior OR-132 rating and dominant recent form (four wins from last five) proves too much for Follow Your Luck to repel.
scenarios.body: Quinlan tracks patiently, waits for Follow Your Luck to weaken approaching the last, then powers clear — Dunkerque's 12/15 strike rate on Good going underscores how comfortable this surface is for him. Despite being in a tracking role, Dunkerque's class ceiling is markedly higher and he may simply have too much for a 5-year-old novice.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Jumping Error Decides
scenarios.trigger: If one runner makes a significant jumping mistake at a critical fence that fundamentally alters the outcome.
scenarios.body: In a two-horse field over fences, a fall or costly error by either runner in the final mile would be decisive — Follow Your Luck, less experienced over fences, carries slightly higher jumping risk. The beneficiary would simply be whichever horse is still standing and travelling, making the winner impossible to predict pre-race.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse — Both Struggle
scenarios.trigger: If the Good ground rides faster than expected and an overly aggressive early tempo leaves Follow Your Luck emptied, with Dunkerque also flat.
scenarios.body: With only two runners, there is no third party to capitalise, making this scenario low-consequence in terms of result change but potentially producing a slow or scrambled finish. In practice, Hughes is too experienced to burn his mount early, making this outcome very unlikely.

watchPoints.text: Watch Follow Your Luck's jumping — as the less experienced chaser in the field, a fence error at a critical point (particularly the downhill fences at Perth) could compromise his lead-holding mission entirely.

Dunkerque's 18-day turnaround is fresh but well within his pattern of winning off similar gaps — no fitness concern flagged, but monitor if he appears flat in the paddock given trainer's poor 14-day record.

With only two runners, any early incident — a stumble, a mistake, a rider error — instantly becomes race-defining in a way it would not be in a full field; stewards' room drama is magnified accordingly.

Follow Your Luck's Going line shows his two wins came on Soft/Soft, not Good — his single Good-ground run was a third, meaning today's conditions are marginally less proven territory for him at this trip.

Brian Hughes's tactical decision on early pace is the fulcrum of this race — if he pings the first few fences and builds a healthy lead, Follow Your Luck's prospects improve significantly; a sluggish start would allow Dunkerque to dominate even before the finish.

races.name: Auto Services Volkswagen Commercial Aftersales Novices' Hurdle Race (GBB Race)
Auto Services Perth 24-Hour Recovery Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Castleheath
runners_data.note: Top-rated runner (OR 119) handled by Sean Bowen and trained by Ciaran Murphy; 2W3P on similar going and a recent second over 2m Good suggest he is in form — a natural hold-up horse who will need the contested early pace to materialise for his finishing kick to matter.

runners_data.name: Scriabin
runners_data.note: Course specialist with 1W and two seconds over this exact course and trip on Good, and one of two confirmed front-runners who will shape the entire race from flag to flag; Patrick Wadge will look to steal a march on Nobotheratall at the break and use the horse's proven track-record here.

runners_data.name: Nobotheratall
runners_data.note: The second confirmed pace-setter, in-form trainer (5/11 over 14 days), and fresh enough at 51 days since last run; won over this trip on Good going at Perth earlier in the season but faces a direct rival for the lead in Scriabin, which may compromise both horses' finishing reserves.

runners_data.name: Try Them
runners_data.note: Four-year-old who has won his last two over this trip on Good and comes in under Brian Hughes, who rides prominently; the youngest in the field but clearly thriving, and his natural tracking position puts him perfectly placed if the front two exhaust each other.

runners_data.name: Inappropriate
runners_data.note: Wears a tongue-tie and cheekpieces, ran 13 days ago (quick turnaround to note), and has a strong profile at this trip on Good ground with 1W4P from 15 similar-going runs; Sean Quinlan will likely settle him just off the pace and hope the contested front plays into his hands in the straight.

runners_data.name: Pure Gold
runners_data.note: Consistent form figure who has finished in the top four in six of his last seven on Good going — his true racing style is at the back, but with so many hold-up types in this field he is unlikely to get the clear passage he needs, which tempers confidence in his finishing run despite the solid profile.

runners_data.name: Just Dottie
runners_data.note: Veteran eight-year-old partnered by claiming rider Miss Becky Smith (7lb), which softens the weight burden and is worth noting; genuine hold-up racer by nature who has been placed at this trip on Good, but the overcrowded rear means she will need an unusually clean passage to land a blow.

runners_data.name: Elemental Eye
runners_data.note: Freshest horse in the field at just 8 days since last run and coming off a decent sequence including a win and a place at this trip — Danny McMenamin trains with Iain Jardine who is 4/27 over 14 days, a modest strike rate; a natural back-marker whose last-to-first style is harder to execute when the hold-up zone is as congested as this race shape creates.

races.paceDynamic: Scriabin and Nobotheratall are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the outset over this 2m Perth trip, creating a genuinely contested early gallop on Good ground rather than a soft lead for either. Scriabin brings strong course form at this trip (1W, 2nd twice over 16f Good at Perth) and is unlikely to concede the front cheaply to Nobotheratall, whose trainer is in good recent form (5/11 over 14 days). The resulting honest, pressure-laden pace should see the lead group race into a headwind of their own making, leaving the closers with a genuine target to pick up — this race shape most clearly favours hold-up or late-running profiles who can track the carnage and pounce from the home turn. The field holds more hold-up types than the race map can accommodate at the rear — Pure Gold, Just Dottie, and Elemental Eye are genuine hold-up horses redistributed into the midfield zone because they are all unlikely to find their natural position with so many genuine back-markers; of these, Elemental Eye (8 days since last run, strong stamina profile) and Pure Gold (consistent course form) are most likely to at least land in mid-division, while Try Them and Castleheath are better placed to exploit the positions the map shows.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested pace, closers pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Scriabin and Nobotheratall fight for the lead and set a pressured honest gallop that softens them both from the third last.
scenarios.body: The two pacemakers race each other into the ground, leaving the field strung out and the final two hurdles to those with reserves; hold-up and prominent types who have settled off the pace arrive with momentum. Castleheath (OR 119, Sean Bowen, 2W3P on similar going) and Try Them (recent winner, Brian Hughes) are ideally positioned to exploit the vacuum.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Scriabin controls and wins
scenarios.trigger: If Scriabin repels Nobotheratall early and settles into an uncontested lead at a regulated gallop, conserving enough for the finish.
scenarios.body: Scriabin has won and placed repeatedly over this course and trip on Good going (9/12 runners on similar going) and if Nobotheratall is checked or settles back, Scriabin can dictate his own rhythm and quicken clear from the last. Patrick Wadge, who knows this horse well, would look to exploit any daylight between the two front-runners early.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent racer outstays all
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fierce enough to break down both leaders but the closers overcook their finishing runs, leaving a prominent-tracking type to pick up the pieces.
scenarios.body: Try Them has finished 1st and 2nd in his last two over this course and trip on identical going, and tracking just off the pace with Brian Hughes in the saddle puts him in the best spot if the leaders tire but the hold-up horses leave it too late. Inappropriate has the form to fill the place positions in this shape, having placed 1st, 2nd, and 3rd in recent starts.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers land late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly searching and every prominent horse is cooked, leaving the genuine back-markers to run through beaten rivals in the final flight.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires Pure Gold, Just Dottie, or Elemental Eye to find their natural hold-up positions and a longer-than-expected gallop to open the race up — with all three redistributed from the true rear, none is guaranteed to get the clear run they need. Elemental Eye is freshest (8 days, recent winner at 12f) and most likely to benefit if chaos unfolds late, but this remains the least probable shape given the overcrowded hold-up zone.

watchPoints.text: Scriabin and Nobotheratall will lock horns for the lead from the off — watch the first two hurdles to see if either yields, because if neither does the pace could be fierce enough to compromise every runner drawn into racing prominently.

Elemental Eye runs just 8 days after his last start, which is a short turnaround for a jumper — monitor his movement in the pre-parade ring and watch for any sign of residual fatigue in the early stages.

Pure Gold, Just Dottie, and Elemental Eye are all genuine hold-up horses crowded into a congested rear — watch for traffic problems turning for home if all three are seeking the same gap between tiring rivals at the same moment.

Try Them is the only four-year-old in the field taking on older, handicap-seasoned horses — Brian Hughes will need to position him off the pace quickly to avoid being trapped wide if the two front-runners immediately dictate a fierce tempo on the inner.

Castleheath is the top weight (168lbs) and top-rated (OR 119) — Sean Bowen will likely hunt cover early and commit his challenge no sooner than the second-last, so watch how cleanly he travels through the early stages as a guide to how the race shape is unfolding.

races.name: Auto Services Mercedes Benz Truck Aftersales Handicap Steeple Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Regal Renaissance
runners_data.note: Proven front-runner with a stellar recent record (three wins from last four including back-to-back over similar trips on Good), Sean Bowen is a major asset, and similar-going form reads 3W7P — the unchallenged lead is his to lose over 3m here.

runners_data.name: Wasdell Dundalk
runners_data.note: An 11-year-old hold-up performer whose recent form reads 4-642P and who hasn't won in similar going across his last 15 attempts; Callum Bewley takes over but the age and declining form are concerns at this trip.

runners_data.name: No Regrets
runners_data.note: Nicky Richards has a 1/2 T14 strike rate and this 12-year-old brings genuine 3m credentials — two of his last five starts came at 2m4f with the best runs on Good, and his last two finishes of 1 and 2 suggest he retains ability, though 93 days off is a flag worth monitoring.

runners_data.name: Inis Oirr
runners_data.note: Recent form of 91-223 suggests consistency without a win being imminent; this is a natural rear-runner who is mapped to midfield only because the field is stacked with hold-up types, so expect Gregor Walkingshaw (10) to race further back than shown — the style mismatch tempers his winning chance in a shape dominated by the leader.

runners_data.name: Sir Carnegie
runners_data.note: Mickey Bowen's yard is firing at T14 6/23 and Brian Hughes is a key booking; the horse carries headgear (blinkers) and returns quickly on 16 days, but at OR 101 he is the lowest-rated runner and, despite two recent wins, his true hold-up style means he needs the race to fall apart in front of him to win.

races.paceDynamic: Regal Renaissance is the sole confirmed front-runner in this five-horse field and, with no rival likely to genuinely contest the lead, Sean Bowen can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over the 3m trip on Good turf at Perth. The three genuine hold-up types — Wasdell Dundalk, No Regrets, and Sir Carnegie — will track from the rear, while Inis Oirr is also a true hold-up horse despite being mapped to midfield for visualisation purposes. With Regal Renaissance able to set his own fractions unchallenged, this race shape strongly favours the prominent-to-front runner who can control the tempo, conserve energy over the fences, and dictate the moment the race quickens from the front — chasers from off the pace will need a genuine stamina test or a jumping error from the leader to get involved. The field holds more hold-up types than can naturally be separated at the rear; of those, Sir Carnegie (Brian Hughes, in-form T14 strike rate) and No Regrets (proven 3m form) are best placed to mount a late challenge if the leader weakens.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Regal Renaissance Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Regal Renaissance bowls along at a comfortable clip and the hold-up brigade are unable to close the gap in the straight.
scenarios.body: Bowen settles Regal Renaissance into a rhythm from the front, jumping fluently and giving nothing away, making the race increasingly hard for hold-up horses to win from off a steady pace; the longer the gallop stays moderate, the more the advantage compounds for the leader.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Stayer Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Regal Renaissance sets a genuinely taxing pace that causes attrition and a hold-up horse picks up the pieces in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: A strong early gallop combined with the 3m distance on Good ground tests the leader's stamina reserves; a horse like No Regrets — proven at 3m and with a recent win — or Sir Carnegie with Brian Hughes timing the challenge can get to the leader when he ties up.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Flurry Overwhelms
scenarios.trigger: If Regal Renaissance makes a critical jumping error or fades sharply inside the final half-mile, leaving the race wide open.
scenarios.body: Without the front-runner controlling proceedings, the hold-up horses converge simultaneously and the outcome depends on which has kept the most in reserve; No Regrets' course-and-distance form and Wasdell Dundalk's consistency over good ground make them dangers in this chaos scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Asserts
scenarios.trigger: If Regal Renaissance loses the lead sooner than expected and a horse tracking closely moves through to win from a mid-pack position.
scenarios.body: Given that Inis Oirr and Sir Carnegie are true hold-up types redistributed forward on the map — racing out of their natural role — their ability to capitalise on this shape is genuinely discounted; this scenario is low probability precisely because no horse in the field naturally wants to sit second and quicken past the leader.

watchPoints.text: Regal Renaissance's jumping must be monitored early — a fall or bad mistake at any of the first few fences is the single event most likely to completely overturn the dominant pace scenario.
No Regrets has been off 93 days and, while Nicky Richards' runners return fit, a first-time-back run over 3m on Good should be kept in mind if he fades in the straight having briefly threatened.

Sir Carnegie's blinkers are a speed-trigger that could push him forward unusually early, potentially creating brief but artificial pace pressure on Regal Renaissance in the first mile before he settles.
Wasdell Dundalk at age 11 with a P (pulled up) on his most recent run warrants monitoring for any signs of distress or jumping errors that could cause interference for runners tracking close behind.

With four genuine hold-up types bunching at the rear, traffic and interference risks increase in the straight if Regal Renaissance tires — watch for horses being baulked as the group converges simultaneously.

races.name: www.asp.scot Stellantis Commercial Aftersales Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Lets Mingle
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner here and likely to lead from the outset; trainer Russell/Scudamore yard 0/3 in past 14 days is a mild concern, and the STYLE_FIT flag (0.94) suggests this isn't her natural role — recent form U-3515 is patchy but the uncontested lead is a genuine tactical asset.

runners_data.name: Follow Charlie
runners_data.note: Two wins from last three runs including back-to-back victories on Good ground over 2m, and the return to a slightly shorter trip than 3m could sharpen him; 5lb claimer Murray Dodd is the query but trainer Smith 2/9 over 14 days gives quiet confidence.

runners_data.name: Spit Spot
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who has the tactical profile to track Lets Mingle closely; 57 days off is a flag, and recent hurdles form has been disappointing (F, P, 6, 7) but wears headgear and is trained by Russell/Scudamore — same 0/3 yard form concern applies.

runners_data.name: Lowlands
runners_data.note: Danny McMenamin-ridden hold-up horse stepping back up beyond 2m where he won last time; Nicky Richards 1/2 in past 14 days is form worth noting, and the horse has placed three times in five similar-going runs — dependent on a strong-enough pace to bring hold-up style into play.

runners_data.name: Bogha Baiste
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up mare with zero wins from seven Good-ground runs; five-year-old taking on older horses, 67 days off, and a form string that reads P334-4 — no win in this company at this trip, and reliant on a strong pace she may not get today.

runners_data.name: Annie Agnew
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with a second in Good-going hurdles in her recent history; amateur rider Mr D McGill (5) is a risk at this level, and trainer Quinn 0/1 in past 14 days offers no encouragement — her handy style suits the race shape if she jumps cleanly.

runners_data.name: Garrick Painter
runners_data.note: Won at 16f on Good ground on most recent run (12 days ago, freshness a plus) but is naturally a hold-up horse positioned in midfield on the map because closing berths are filled — in this race shape he may not get far back enough to deliver his finishing effort cleanly; trainer Kelly 0/14 in 14 days is a damning form line.

runners_data.name: Kinbara Firstdraft
runners_data.note: Last-six form reads 574546 with no win from many attempts, and this genuine hold-up horse is mapped to midfield because the rear is oversubscribed; only nine days since last run (freshness slight plus) but the trajectory and 0/1 trainer form suggest limited upside.

runners_data.name: Hawkseye View
runners_data.note: 149 days off is a significant absence flag; has won on Good ground over 2m before but hurdles form has been inconsistent and prominent style puts her in the mix early — lack of fitness after a long layoff makes this a come-on run rather than a winning one.

runners_data.name: Tigress Lilly
runners_data.note: Young five-year-old with form reading 00-665 — no wins and struggling for quality; a true hold-up horse pushed into midfield by the crowded rear, the STYLE_FIT flag (0.91) signals she won't get her preferred position, and all five career runs have been on shorter trips of 16f.

races.paceDynamic: Lets Mingle is the one confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner 2m4f handicap hurdle and, with no natural rival willing to push up and press from the outset, is set to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good ground at Perth. That measured tempo plays directly into the hands of horses who can sit handy and travel within themselves, preserving energy for a genuine test over the final two hurdles — a prominent-to-midfield profile is the clear tactical beneficiary. Follow Charlie and Lowlands are the most credible late challengers from hold-up positions, but the field holds more genuine hold-up types than can all slot into the rear — Garrick Painter, Kinbara Firstdraft, and Tigress Lilly are true back-of-the-field horses redistributed to midfield on the map because the closing slots are oversubscribed, meaning their ability to produce a clean late run is compromised by their likely position being further forward than ideal. With one front-runner setting a honest but uncontested pace, this race shape most strongly favours runners with prominent or handy racing styles who can track the leader and pounce from the second-last.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lets Mingle Controls, Handy Types Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Lets Mingle leads at a fair but unforced pace and prominent runners track comfortably throughout.
scenarios.body: Lets Mingle sets the race up for those sitting just behind, and when the tempo increases from three out, handy horses like Spit Spot and Annie Agnew are ideally placed to challenge; the Good ground and moderate gallop suits horses who can quicken off a sound surface rather than grind. Follow Charlie, despite a hold-up tag, has the class (two recent wins) to pick up efficiently if ridden more positively than usual.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Follow Charlie Swoops from Hold-Up
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and Follow Charlie's jockey (claim 5lb) gets a dream passage through.
scenarios.body: Follow Charlie has won twice recently on Good ground over 2m and drops back in trip slightly from 3m, giving him a fitness and freshness edge; if gaps appear in the straight he has the class to cut through late. His trainer is in form (2/9 over 14 days) and the 5lb claim from Murray Dodd is a meaningful booking.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Lowlands Delivers Hold-Up Run
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is honest enough that the front rank tires and Lowlands, stepping back up in trip, finds a clean run.
scenarios.body: Lowlands won over 2m and has placed twice over further, and Nicky Richards is 1/2 in the past 14 days suggesting stable form; Danny McMenamin is an accomplished claimer who could produce him late with a good racing position. However, the likely controlled pace makes a deep hold-up challenge the least comfortable scenario, and the redistributed closers further crowd the back of the field.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Lets Mingle is left completely alone and the pace proves so slow that no one can reel her in from the last.
scenarios.body: In a race where hold-up horses are forced into unfamiliar prominent positions, Lets Mingle could exploit the resulting chaos and a flat pace by simply staying on the bridle and quickening clear from two out. Good ground suits her confirmed stamina base and she has placed at this track before, but a STYLE_FIT flag (0.94) and recent form (U-3515) tempers confidence sharply.

watchPoints.text: Lets Mingle leads entirely unchallenged — if no one goes with her from the front she could dictate a pace so slow that every hold-up horse is left with too much to do late.

Garrick Painter, Kinbara Firstdraft, and Tigress Lilly are all natural hold-up horses compressed into midfield positions — watch for traffic congestion approaching the home turn as several riders seek the same ground simultaneously.

Follow Charlie's jockey Murray Dodd claims 5lb but has limited opportunities at this level — any hesitation in finding a gap between the last two hurdles could cost a hold-up horse with genuine class the winning chance.

Hawkseye View returns after 149 days off — monitor her market drift late to gauge stable confidence, as a forward move could signal fitness, while a big drift would confirm this is a race-fitness exercise.

Trainer Lucinda Russell & Michael Scudamore saddle three runners (Lets Mingle, Spit Spot, Tigress Lilly) but are 0/3 over the past 14 days — watch for any reported stable issues or whether the market separates one of their trio as a banker.

races.name: Auto Services Perth Sales And Rentals Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Down Around
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with strong Good-ground credentials (2W5P in similar going, sim-going 13/15), won over 26f at Perth last time out and steps up to 3m from a 7-day turnaround under Sean Bowen for Gordon Elliott's powerful operation; blinkers on and the combination of elite trainer, top jockey, and ideal race position makes him the standout shape beneficiary.

runners_data.name: Midnight Moonshine
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type whose recent form (0-9-0-5-6) gives little encouragement, though she handles Good ground and gets the trip; the amateur claimer (7lb) is a negative in a competitive handicap and she will need gaps to appear that this pace map is unlikely to create.

runners_data.name: Sauce Of Life
runners_data.note: Prominent racer fitted with a hood, trained by Nicky Richards whose yard is 1/2 in the 14-day window; the 86-day absence is a slight flag on an 11-year-old, but he won over 20f on Soft and his prominent style suits this solo-lead scenario well if fitness is intact.

runners_data.name: Dalileo
runners_data.note: Back-to-back 24f wins on Good ground for this 11-year-old make him interesting on pure form, and he arrives just 23 days since last running; a true hold-up type by style, meaning he is reliant on the race developing a late-run scenario that the current pace structure is not strongly set up to provide.

runners_data.name: Theirshegoes
runners_data.note: Decent recent second at 24f on Good gives him a form profile worth noting, but he is a genuine hold-up horse displaced into a midfield map position — he is unlikely to get the true position his style demands here, which materially tempers his chance; the 54-day absence adds a further layer of uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Le Grand Vert
runners_data.note: Won at 25f and placed at 26f on Good, so the trip and surface are not concerns, and Sean Quinlan is a capable jockey; however, this is a true hold-up horse pushed forward on the map by field composition, and the 10-day turnaround following a recent run that produced a sixth suggests he is not in top form.

runners_data.name: C'Mon So
runners_data.note: The youngest in the field at five and a hold-up type by nature, C'Mon So has failed to trouble the judge in seven runs with no wins and no places on Good ground specifically; the 67-day absence and lowest OR in the field (79) compound a profile that does not suit this race shape.

runners_data.name: Burgundy Man
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner, he has not won in five visible starts but shapes the entire race by leading; Toby Wynne takes over for the R Mike Smith yard (2/9 in 14 days) and if he is allowed to dictate at a comfortable gallop, he could prove very difficult to catch, though his completion record has been patchy.

races.paceDynamic: Burgundy Man is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 3m Perth hurdle on Good ground, and with no rival likely to dispute his lead from flag to finish, he is set to control proceedings at a pace entirely of his own choosing — sustainable, unhurried, and potentially race-shaping. Down Around and Sauce Of Life are the two genuine prominent types who will track him, meaning the real race will be run out from second and third throughout rather than at the head of affairs. This field actually contains a heavy cluster of hold-up horses — Theirshegoes, Le Grand Vert, and C'Mon So are true hold-up types but have been mapped to midfield because there is nowhere else to place them, and none of them are likely to get the true position their style demands in this compressed shape. The race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can travel efficiently behind a solo leader and pounce before the hold-up horses get into the race, making Down Around and Sauce Of Life the primary beneficiaries of this configuration.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Burgundy Man Leads, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Burgundy Man sets a genuine but unhurried tempo and the prominent horses travel comfortably before the last
scenarios.body: Burgundy Man dictates on his own terms from the front, keeping the race honest enough to expose hold-up horses but controlled enough to reward those who track him; Down Around and Sauce Of Life, both prominent types with good Good-ground records, are ideally positioned to pounce at the third-last.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Burgundy Man is allowed to dictate at a truly modest pace and builds an unassailable lead before rivals can respond
scenarios.body: With no pace pressure whatsoever, Burgundy Man could bounce along in front and simply not be reeled in, particularly if the hold-up horses are bottled up in midfield traffic and can never get to him; his 0W5P record suggests he is competitive without winning but this configuration maximises his chance.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Dalileo Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final mile and hold-up horses get a clear run for home
scenarios.body: Dalileo has won twice at 24f on Good and arrives on the back of back-to-back wins, and if the field strings out and gaps appear, Peter Kavanagh can produce him with a late challenge; however this depends on a race shape that does not strongly favour hold-up runners given the pace dynamic.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Runners Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses dramatically and the redistributed midfield horses find racing room to finish strongly
scenarios.body: Theirshegoes, Le Grand Vert, and C'Mon So are all true hold-up types racing out of role in this shape, making a scenario dependent on them genuinely unlikely; Midnight Moonshine, a genuine hold-up type, is best placed of this group but her form figures offer limited confidence.

watchPoints.text: Burgundy Man's gallop from the front is the race-shaping factor — if he quickens going away from the back straight, watch whether Down Around and Sauce Of Life have the pace reserves to close, because the hold-up horses behind them almost certainly will not.

Sauce Of Life's 86-day absence at age 11 is a fitness flag — if he travels poorly early under Danny McMenamin and drops away before the final mile, the prominent side of the race loses a key player and Dalileo's closing chance improves.

Theirshegoes, Le Grand Vert, and C'Mon So are all genuine hold-up horses squeezed into a midfield role by field composition — watch for traffic problems on the final bend if they are all tracking each other and none can find a clear passage.

Dalileo's back-to-back wins give him the best recent winning form in the race, but Peter Kavanagh will need a gap to appear from the three-out flight — watch whether the prominent horses clear enough space for him to thread through.

Gordon Elliott's T14 strike rate (2/35) looks modest in raw terms but his runners are rarely non-triers; with Sean Bowen booked, Down Around arriving fresh off a Perth win and stepping up in trip, watch for him to be produced with purpose from the third-last.
